sentences.zh: 我是来自《99% Invisible》的 Roman Mars。

sentences.en: Ben Brock Johnson from Endless Thread.
sentences.zh: 我是来自《Endless Thread》的 Ben Brock Johnson。

sentences.en: Here we are, final boss of Hidden Levels.
sentences.zh: 我们到了，《Hidden Levels》的最终关卡。

sentences.en: Do you have all your legendary items?
sentences.zh: 你带上所有传奇装备了吗？

sentences.en: Did you save the game in case we lose against the final boss?
sentences.zh: 你存过档了吗？万一我们打不过最终BOSS呢？
这确实是个重要的考量。

sentences.en: Yes, I am so excited for this because I think this might be the first final boss I've ever encountered.
sentences.zh: 是的，我太兴奋了，因为我觉得这可能是我遇到过的第一个最终BOSS。

sentences.en: Like, I've never reached the part of the video game that you actually hit the final boss.
sentences.zh: 就像是，我从来没玩到过电子游戏里真正面对最终BOSS的那一部分。

sentences.en: So this is thrilling for me to be here at the very end.
sentences.zh: 所以能来到这最后一步，让我感到非常激动。

sentences.en: Well, get ready to have a huge sense of accomplishment for beating a final boss that maybe means nothing to anyone except for you.
sentences.zh: 那么，准备好迎接巨大的成就感吧，去击败一个可能对别人毫无意义，但对你却意义非凡的最终BOSS。

sentences.en: That's a very video game feeling.
sentences.zh: 这非常有电子游戏的感觉。

sentences.en: Let's talk about something we've been touching on through this series but maybe never said explicitly.
sentences.zh: 让我们聊聊我们在这一系列节目中一直触及，但可能从未明确说出来的话题。

sentences.en: How does that sit with you, Roman?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这个说法怎么样，Roman？

sentences.en: It sits very well with me.
I think video games are absolutely art.
sentences.zh: 我认为电子游戏绝对是艺术。

sentences.en: They have beautiful visions that bring worlds alive for people.
sentences.zh: 它们拥有美丽的愿景，为人们赋予了鲜活的世界。

sentences.en: They teach people how to think.
sentences.zh: 它们教会人们如何思考。

sentences.en: The video games are absolutely art.
And just like other kinds of art, video games are full of reference and homage.
sentences.zh: 就像其他艺术形式一样，电子游戏充满了引用和致敬。

sentences.en: So, for instance, I think maybe you've heard of the game Metal Gear or Metal Gear Solid, that series of games.
sentences.zh: 比如，我想你可能听说过《合金装备》（Metal Gear）或《合金装备》（Metal Gear Solid）那个系列游戏。

sentences.en: But Metal Gear, I'm aware of Metal Gear.
So, Metal Gear was created nearly 40 years ago by game designer Hideo Kojima.
sentences.zh: 《合金装备》是游戏设计师小岛秀夫（Hideo Kojima）在近40年前创作的。

sentences.en: Kojima is now one of the most loved and respected auteurs of video games in part because he has always put his own personality into the games that he makes.
sentences.zh: 小岛秀夫现在是游戏界最受爱戴和尊敬的作者之一，部分原因是他总是将自己的个性融入到他制作的游戏中。

sentences.en: Even when they're basically referencing other pieces of art.
sentences.zh: 即使当这些想法本质上是在引用其他艺术作品时也是如此。

sentences.en: The main character, Roman, in Metal Gear, Metal Gear Solid is named Solid Snake.
sentences.zh: Roman，在《合金装备》和《合金装备》系列中，主角的名字叫 Solid Snake（索利德·斯内克）。

sentences.en: Solid Snake, he wears an eye patch.
He's got a stubble beard on his Chad-like jaw.
sentences.zh: 他那像查德（Chad）一样的下巴上留着胡茬。

sentences.en: When you look at this game character, Roman, does he look familiar to you?
sentences.zh: 当你看着这个游戏角色时，Roman，你觉得他眼熟吗？

sentences.en: So, I'm looking at a picture of Solid Snake and he is a dead ringer for Snake Plissken from the movie Escape from New York.
sentences.zh: 我正在看 Solid Snake 的照片，他简直和电影《逃出纽约》（Escape from New York）里的 Snake Plissken 一模一样。

sentences.en: I think we'd have very few arguments on movie night, Roman.
sentences.zh: 我想我们在电影之夜应该不会有什么争论，Roman。
确实是一部伟大的电影。

sentences.en: Solid Snake was inspired by Snake Plissken.
sentences.zh: Solid Snake 的灵感正是来自 Snake Plissken。

sentences.en: As you say, the character played by Kurt Russell in that 1981 sci-fi classic.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，那是1981年科幻经典电影中由库尔特·拉塞尔（Kurt Russell）饰演的角色。

sentences.en: You gonna kill me now, Snake?
So, Kojima is obviously like a movie fan.
sentences.zh: 所以，小岛秀夫显然是个影迷。

sentences.en: And Kojima actually has this new set of games that is also turning into their own franchise.
sentences.zh: 而且小岛秀夫现在还有一套新的游戏，也正在发展成自己的系列。

sentences.en: Okay, well, those are new to me.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这些对我来说是新东西。

sentences.en: I've never heard of Death Stranding.
sentences.zh: 我从没听说过《死亡搁浅》。

sentences.en: So, this game goes further than just references and homage.
sentences.zh: 所以，这款游戏不仅仅是引用和致敬。

sentences.en: The game has been described as sort of a walking simulator.
sentences.zh: 这款游戏被描述为一种“步行模拟器”。

sentences.en: Because the main character is not a warrior.
He's not a smash-em-bash-em kind of guy.
sentences.zh: 他不是那种横冲直撞的家伙。

sentences.en: So, in the game, you are delivering packages.
sentences.zh: 在游戏里，你就是在送包裹。

sentences.en: This does seem like my kind of game.
sentences.zh: 这看起来确实是我会喜欢的游戏类型。

sentences.en: I'm having a hard time imagining why a game about a courier is called Death Stranding.
sentences.zh: 我很难想象为什么一个关于快递员的游戏叫《死亡搁浅》。

sentences.en: That doesn't quite make sense to me.
I mean, it does all take place in a post-apocalyptic environment.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，故事确实发生在一个后启示录的环境中。

sentences.en: The stakes are high when you're delivering babies in a post-apocalyptic environment.
sentences.zh: 在后启示录环境中运送婴儿，赌注当然很高。

sentences.en: Yeah, and, you know, we're laughing about this, but the game is also like a piece of commentary.
sentences.zh: 是啊，虽然我们对此付之一笑，但这款游戏也是一种评论。

sentences.en: You can see Kojima thinking through big questions, like the dangers of living in a society where we barely physically interact.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到小岛秀夫在思考一些宏大的问题，比如生活在一个我们几乎没有身体接触的社会中的危险。

sentences.en: And he's doing it through this delivery guy, this courier in Death Stranding.
sentences.zh: 而他正是通过《死亡搁浅》里的这个送货员来表达的。

sentences.en: So, Kojima is an example of how an artist's personality, their point of view, can get coded right into the game itself.
sentences.zh: 所以，小岛秀夫是一个很好的例子，说明了艺术家的个性、他们的观点，是如何被编码进游戏本身的。

sentences.en: And today, Roman, we're going to talk about another one of these examples, a game really coming from the inside of one man's brain, his anxieties, his hopes,
sentences.zh: 今天，Roman，我们要谈谈另一个这样的例子，一款真正源自一个人大脑内部的游戏，包含了他的焦虑、他的希望，

sentences.en: his fears about the industry he works in and the company he works for.
sentences.zh: 以及他对所处行业和所效力公司的恐惧。

sentences.en: This is where we're going to start our final boss episode of Hidden Levels with a Sega employee who had a front row seat to all of the chaos of working in the gaming business in the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 这就是我们《Hidden Levels》最终关卡要开始的地方，讲述一位世嘉（Sega）员工的故事，他亲历了90年代游戏行业工作的种种混乱。

sentences.en: And we're going to learn how he turned his experience into the most strangely iconic meta video game maybe of all time.
sentences.zh: 我们将了解他是如何将自己的经历转化为史上最离奇、最具标志性的元游戏（meta video game）之一。

sentences.en: 99PI producer Jason DeLeon brings it home for us.
sentences.zh: 99PI制作人 Jason DeLeon 为我们带来这个故事。

sentences.en: When I first met Tez O'Kano, I wasn't sure what to expect.
sentences.zh: 当我第一次见到 Tez O'Kano 时，我不知道该期待什么。

sentences.en: I had reached out to talk about a video game he created nearly 25 years ago.
sentences.zh: 我联系他是为了聊聊他近25年前创作的一款电子游戏。

sentences.en: An obscure and fun Japanese title that had become a sort of fixation of mine.
sentences.zh: 那是一款冷门但有趣的游戏，成了我的一种执念。

sentences.en: It's a game that you can't really begin to understand until you get to know the person who made it.
sentences.zh: 这是一款在你真正了解创作者本人之前，无法真正理解的游戏。

sentences.en: And I live in Tokyo currently and have lived in Tokyo for a while, but I am not a Tokyo person.
sentences.zh: 我现在住在东京，也住了一段时间了，但我不是个“东京人”。

sentences.en: Through an interpreter, O'Kano told me about his early life in rural southern Japan and how growing up in the 1970s, just as video games were taking off,
sentences.zh: 通过翻译，O'Kano 告诉了我他在日本南部农村的早年生活，以及在70年代电子游戏刚兴起时成长，

sentences.en: set the stage for everything that was to come.
sentences.zh: 是如何为后来的一切奠定基础的。

sentences.en: Like, I really have to insist on it.

sentences.zh: 那里什么都没有，真的是什么都没有。

sentences.en: In terms of entertainment, what we had was like the great outdoors.
sentences.zh: 说到娱乐，我们有的只是大自然。

sentences.en: So, anything with a hint of, you know, the city lingering on it was just something that we all like longed for.
sentences.zh: 所以，任何带有一点点城市气息的东西，都是我们所有人所向往的。

sentences.en: As a kid, O'Kano dreamed of leaving the countryside.
sentences.zh: 小时候，O'Kano 梦想着离开乡村。

sentences.en: But often, video games were his closest escape.
sentences.zh: 但通常，电子游戏是他最亲近的逃避方式。

sentences.en: He remembers playing versions of the classic tennis and brick breaker titles of the 70s, which were fun, but those games didn't really move him.
sentences.zh: 他记得玩过70年代经典的网球和打砖块游戏的版本，虽然有趣，但那些游戏并没有真正打动他。

sentences.en: He says his love really started when one iconic title landed in his hometown.
sentences.zh: 他说他的热爱真正开始于一款标志性游戏登陆他家乡的时候。

sentences.en: When O'Kano first played Space Invaders, he was struck by something he had never experienced in a game before.
sentences.zh: 当 O'Kano 第一次玩《太空侵略者》时，他被一种从未在游戏中体验过的东西震撼了。

sentences.en: Some people might only see an 11x5 grid of pixelated aliens when they play Space Invaders, but O'Kano saw a whole new world.
sentences.zh: 有些人玩《太空侵略者》时可能只看到11x5的像素外星人网格，但 O'Kano 看到的是一个全新的世界。

sentences.en: And that passion led him away from the countryside and into a university where he studied game design.
sentences.zh: 这份热情引领他离开了乡村，进入大学学习游戏设计。

sentences.en: As a student, O'Kano created games on MSX, a type of home computer that helped shape the 80s Japanese gaming scene.
sentences.zh: 作为学生，O'Kano 在 MSX 上创作游戏，这是一种塑造了80年代日本游戏场景的家用电脑。
MSX 是一款很棒的游戏机。

sentences.en: Like, I love, love, love MSX.
sentences.zh: 我是说，我爱、爱、爱死 MSX 了。

sentences.en: It's burned into my brain making games like that.
sentences.zh: 制作那样的游戏已经刻进了我的脑海里。

sentences.en: One of O'Kano's MSX games was a silly 8-bit shoot-em-up called Salad Man.
sentences.zh: O'Kano 的 MSX 游戏之一是一款愚蠢的8位射击游戏，叫《Salad Man》。

sentences.en: The game was a spoof of a famous Japanese game called Salamander.
sentences.zh: 这款游戏是对日本著名游戏《Salamander》的恶搞。

sentences.en: MSX magazine wrote about Salad Man and said it was funny and kind of crazy.
sentences.zh: MSX 杂志曾写过《Salad Man》，说它很有趣，而且有点疯狂。

sentences.en: And ultimately, that playful, oddball spirit helped O'Kano land the job straight out of college at Sega.
sentences.zh: 最终，这种顽皮、古怪的精神帮助 O'Kano 在大学毕业后直接进入了世嘉工作。

sentences.en: And, you know, like, you can see, you can tell that I'm kind of a weird guy.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你可以看出来，我确实是个怪人。

sentences.en: At the time, the company was riding high on the success of the Sega Genesis.
sentences.zh: 当时，公司正处于世嘉 Genesis 成功的巅峰期。

sentences.en: It was the first console to challenge Nintendo's grip over the home gaming industry.
sentences.zh: 这是第一台挑战任天堂在家用游戏行业统治地位的游戏机。

sentences.en: This kicked off what we know today as the Console Wars,
sentences.zh: 这开启了我们今天所知的“主机战争”，

sentences.en: a decades-long competition between companies for gaming supremacy.
sentences.zh: 这是各公司之间为争夺游戏霸权而进行的数十年竞争。

sentences.en: Early on, Sega and Nintendo competed over who had the better 2D graphics.
sentences.zh: 早期，世嘉和任天堂在谁拥有更好的2D图形上展开竞争。

sentences.en: But by the mid-90s, video games were heading in a new direction.
sentences.zh: 但到了90年代中期，电子游戏正朝着一个新的方向发展。

sentences.en: Right after I started working there, like, it was, everything was 3D.
sentences.zh: 我刚开始在那里工作时，一切都变成了3D。

sentences.en: You want to do pixel art or anything pixel, anything flat, no, it's over.
sentences.zh: 你想做像素艺术或任何像素、任何平面的东西？不，结束了。

sentences.en: You can't sell that kind of stuff.
When O'Kano created Salad Man, he had to meticulously draw and color each individual graphic.
sentences.zh: 当 O'Kano 创作《Salad Man》时，他必须一丝不苟地绘制和着色每一个独立的图形。

sentences.en: On MSX, this meant following a strict set of rules on the number of pixels he could use
sentences.zh: 在 MSX 上，这意味着要遵循一套严格的规则，包括他能使用的像素数量

sentences.en: But 3D required a very different skill set.
sentences.zh: 但3D需要一套完全不同的技能。

sentences.en: So, when he arrived at Sega, O'Kano recalls that a bunch of pixel artists suddenly needed
sentences.zh: 所以，当他来到世嘉时，O'Kano 回忆说，一群像素艺术家突然需要

sentences.en: to adapt, or they might find themselves out of work.
sentences.zh: 做出调整，否则他们可能会失业。

sentences.en: And that really rubbed me the wrong way.
You know, I got into games because I like pixel art.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我进入游戏行业是因为我喜欢像素艺术。

sentences.en: But by the time I got my start in this industry, the world of pixels was already on its way out.
sentences.zh: 但当我开始在这个行业工作时，像素世界已经开始走下坡路了。

sentences.en: Okano feared that with the whole industry pushing towards 3D, pixel artists like him
sentences.zh: 冈野担心，随着整个行业都在向 3D 转型，像他这样的像素艺术家

sentences.en: would become a thing of the paSt.
He described it to me as watching the collapse of an empire.
sentences.zh: 他向我形容那感觉就像是在目睹一个帝国的崩塌。

sentences.en: Sega couldn't be concerned with all that meticulously drawn, color-each-pixel, artsy-fartsy stuff.
sentences.zh: 世嘉没法顾及那些精雕细琢、逐像素上色、华而不实的东西。

sentences.en: They needed to innovate or risk falling behind their rivals.
sentences.zh: 他们必须创新，否则就有被竞争对手甩在后面的风险。

sentences.en: But in Sega's push to bring new technology and 3D gaming into homes,
sentences.zh: 但在世嘉将新技术和 3D 游戏引入家庭的推动过程中，

sentences.en: the company just kept screwing up.
For example, are you a fan of Marky Mark and the Funky Bunch?
sentences.zh: 比如，你是 Marky Mark and the Funky Bunch 的粉丝吗？

sentences.en: Here's a game Sega put out on the Sega CD, where you make Mark Wahlberg's music video.
sentences.zh: 这是世嘉在世嘉 CD 上推出的一款游戏，你可以制作马克·沃尔伯格的音乐录影带。

sentences.en: You want to make my video?
You know, give me more shots of Marky with his shirt off.
sentences.zh: 你知道，多给我一些 Marky 脱掉衬衫的镜头。

sentences.en: The Sega CD was an add-on to the Genesis that tried to cash in on the popularity of CDs at the time.
sentences.zh: 世嘉 CD 是 Genesis 的一个附加组件，旨在利用当时 CD 的流行来赚钱。

sentences.en: But the device just didn't have many games.
sentences.zh: 但这个设备本身并没有多少游戏。

sentences.en: And big surprise, the Marky Mark one wasn't flying off the shelf.
sentences.zh: 而且不出所料，Marky Mark 的那款游戏根本卖不动。

sentences.en: Sega followed this debacle up with yet another doomed piece of hardware called the 32X.
sentences.zh: 世嘉在这次惨败后，又推出了一款注定失败的硬件，叫 32X。

sentences.en: It was a device that you literally stuck into the top of your Genesis to supercharge its processing power.
sentences.zh: 这是一款你直接插在 Genesis 顶部来增强其处理能力的设备。

sentences.en: Just stick it in your Genesis.
sentences.zh: 把它插进你的 Genesis 就行了。

sentences.en: The 32X was too little too late.
People were ready to move on from the Genesis.
sentences.zh: 人们已经准备好告别 Genesis 了。

sentences.en: They were ready for a true 3D console.
sentences.zh: 他们准备好迎接真正的 3D 主机了。

sentences.en: But the company's next system, the Sega Saturn, totally missed the mark.
sentences.zh: 但该公司的下一代系统——世嘉土星，完全没能达到预期。

sentences.en: So the Sega Saturn is really a machine that's very, very good at moving sprites,
sentences.zh: 世嘉土星其实是一台非常、非常擅长移动精灵图的机器，

sentences.en: so that's the 2D bits of art, around a screen very, very quickly.
sentences.zh: 也就是那些 2D 艺术素材，在屏幕上移动得非常、非常快。
但它处理 3D 的能力就没那么强了。

sentences.en: And this is a miscalculation on Sega's part because by the mid-90s, everyone wants 3D games.
sentences.zh: 这是世嘉的一次误判，因为到了 90 年代中期，每个人都想要 3D 游戏。

sentences.en: This is Simon Parkin, a game journalist and host of the podcast My Perfect Console.
sentences.zh: 这位是西蒙·帕金，游戏记者，也是播客《我完美的主机》的主持人。

sentences.en: Simon says, haha, that with each new piece of hardware, Sega further confused and alienated their audience.
sentences.zh: 西蒙说，哈哈，随着每一款新硬件的推出，世嘉进一步困惑并疏远了他们的受众。

sentences.en: After all, the company hyped the Saturn as an era-defining 3D console.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，公司曾大肆宣传土星是一款定义时代的 3D 主机。

sentences.en: But when they couldn't deliver the goods, a total newcomer to the industry stepped in and did.
sentences.zh: 但当他们无法兑现承诺时，一位行业新秀介入并做到了。

sentences.en: Sony's PlayStation is the first really, really capable 3D machine.
sentences.zh: 索尼的 PlayStation 是第一台真正、真正有能力的 3D 机器。

sentences.en: The PlayStation was Sony's first console, and it was a massive hit,
sentences.zh: PlayStation 是索尼的第一台主机，它取得了巨大的成功，

sentences.en: selling tens of millions of consoles worldwide.
sentences.zh: 在全球卖出了数千万台。

sentences.en: Pair that with the release of the Nintendo 64, another console with 3D graphics,
sentences.zh: 再加上任天堂 64 的发布，另一款拥有 3D 图形的主机，

sentences.en: and suddenly, Sega was in crisis.
sentences.zh: 突然之间，世嘉陷入了危机。

sentences.en: The high times of the Genesis were only a few years in the rearview,
sentences.zh: Genesis 的辉煌时期才过去几年，

sentences.en: but it was fair to ask if Sega was going the way of Marky Mark and the Funky Bunch.
sentences.zh: 但人们不禁要问，世嘉是否正在重蹈 Marky Mark and the Funky Bunch 的覆辙。

sentences.en: Gone were the good vibrations, and so long went to sweet sensations.
sentences.zh: 美好的共鸣已逝，甜蜜的感觉也随之而去。

sentences.en: Sega needed to hit the reset button.
And that's exactly what they did with the DreamcaSt.
sentences.zh: 而这正是他们用 Dreamcast 所做的事情。

sentences.en: The ads emphasize, you know, firstly, an apology, almoSt.
sentences.zh: 广告强调的，你知道，首先几乎是一种道歉。

sentences.en: Like, sorry for how far Sega has fallen.

sentences.en: The Dreamcast was Sega's response to the PlayStation,

sentences.zh: 并将最近动荡的过去抛在身后。

sentences.en: So, yeah, this is the gamble that Sega is making.
